L01.why: Comma after 'undetectable' then 'after sunset the' likely joins two independent clauses with a comma splice; but depends on unseen sentence.

L02.why: Infinitive is the odd form out among finite verbs and participle; but any could fit depending on subject and structure.

L03.why: Pure agreement/tense item; no option is wrong without knowing the subject's number and the passage tense.

L04.why: Relative 'which the' structurally different; period, semicolon, colon are often all equivalent so one of B or colon must be key.

L05.why: No punctuation lets 'cools a seed crystal' misread as transitive or fuse clauses; still possible if clause is not independent.

L06.why: Comma before restrictive 'that' (or comma splice with demonstrative 'that') is never accepted SEC usage.

L07.why: Comma likely creates a splice; but could precede an appositive or dependent element, so not certain.

L08.why: 'cue, that whatever' is an awkward comma plus 'that' construction; appositive noun clause is possible but unlikely.

L09.why: 'whereupon' is a marked, rare connector; but all four are grammatical structures depending on what follows.

L10.why: Agreement/tense item; correctness depends entirely on the unseen subject and time frame.

L11.why: Dangling-modifier item; 'a visiting botanist' introduces new actor, plausibly mismatched; true subject depends on the withheld modifier.

L12.why: who/whom depends on whether a verb or infinitive follows 'considered'; tense depends on context. Nothing decidable from options.
